hook: The trumpet sounds and everyone looks up. This time, the question is how you will respond.

sections.title: Who calls, and who answers?
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Above, an angel emerges from clouds, its red wings outspread, blowing a golden trumpet angled downwards. A white banner with a red cross hangs from it. Below, grey-white figures rise from open rectangular coffins, looking up and reaching towards the sky.

An adult stands on each side of the foreground, with a smaller figure between them, back turned to the viewer. Farther away is another group, also raising their arms. Water and a mountain range give the scene depth. This is not a picture of one person standing alone to be reprimanded. The trumpet’s summons and the bodies reaching upwards in response form a collective transformation. [View Judgement](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_20_Judgement.jpg).

sections.title: The title is Judgement; Waite’s emphasis is transformation
sections.bodyMarkdown:
In Part II, Waite retains the religious imagery of the Last Judgement and resurrection, while stressing the figures’ shared wonder, devotion and joy. He interprets the card as transformation accomplished in response to a higher summons, heard and answered inwardly as well. This is his mystical interpretation, not evidence that a reader has received a supernatural command. [Waite on Judgement](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar20.htm).

His Part III entry includes a change of position, renewal and outcome. The reversed list contains weakness but also deliberation and decision, rather than punishment alone. [Waite’s divinatory meanings](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm).

sections.title: Review the past in order to give a new answer
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Our upright reading concerns a point that needs a definite response. What happened, what part you played, and what you want to do next belong in the same view. This might involve acknowledging a mistake, choosing a different direction, or accepting that you have changed. Alongside concern about how others will judge you, ask which facts already support a decision.

Reversed, the card may describe knowing a reply is needed but delaying through endless preparation. It can also suggest turning reflection into relentless self-blame, leaving no room to act again. Distinguish “I still need information” from “I have enough information, but fear taking responsibility for the consequences”. The first calls for further checking; the second for smaller steps you can take responsibility for.

sections.title: In everyday situations
sections.bodyMarkdown:
**Career.** After a period in a role, you become increasingly certain that you do not want to keep doing the same duties. Write down the relevant experiences, acceptable conditions and possible next steps, then decide whether to discuss changes or explore another direction.

**Repairing a relationship.** You realise that an earlier response hurt a friend. Renewal can begin by acknowledging the specific behaviour and hearing how it affected them. Saying “I understand now” does not entitle you to immediate forgiveness.

**A review.** A project ends, and everyone wants to move on quickly. Describe recurring mistakes and agree who will take responsibility in future. That gives reflection a new outcome, rather than making one person the target of every accusation.

sections.title: Try it for yourself
sections.bodyMarkdown: Write a five-sentence reply to your future self: what happened, what you acknowledge, what you will stop excusing, what you can repair, and when you will take the first step. Keep each sentence about actions, rather than labels for your character.

sections.title: Common misreadings
sections.bodyMarkdown: Judgement does not pronounce you guilty, or guarantee the return of an old relationship or a particular person. Rising again can help us think about renewal, but reconciliation in real life still requires both people’s willingness.

- Death: Compare the ending of a stage with the answer you give to a new life after it.
- The World: Notice how a definite response can lead towards completing a stage.

articleMarkdown:
# XX Judgement: Hear what needs an answer

**Upright, at a glance:** Some things can’t stay vague. Look back clearly, then make a decision.

**Reversed, at a glance:** You may be avoiding a response, or blaming yourself so much that deciding feels impossible.

Keywords: Awakening · Response · Renewal

The trumpet sounds and everyone looks up. This time, the question is how you will respond.

## Who calls, and who answers?

Above, an angel emerges from clouds, its red wings outspread, blowing a golden trumpet angled downwards. A white banner with a red cross hangs from it. Below, grey-white figures rise from open rectangular coffins, looking up and reaching towards the sky.

An adult stands on each side of the foreground, with a smaller figure between them, back turned to the viewer. Farther away is another group, also raising their arms. Water and a mountain range give the scene depth. This is not a picture of one person standing alone to be reprimanded. The trumpet’s summons and the bodies reaching upwards in response form a collective transformation. [View Judgement](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_20_Judgement.jpg).

## The title is Judgement; Waite’s emphasis is transformation

In Part II, Waite retains the religious imagery of the Last Judgement and resurrection, while stressing the figures’ shared wonder, devotion and joy. He interprets the card as transformation accomplished in response to a higher summons, heard and answered inwardly as well. This is his mystical interpretation, not evidence that a reader has received a supernatural command. [Waite on Judgement](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar20.htm).

His Part III entry includes a change of position, renewal and outcome. The reversed list contains weakness but also deliberation and decision, rather than punishment alone. [Waite’s divinatory meanings](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm).

## Review the past in order to give a new answer

Our upright reading concerns a point that needs a definite response. What happened, what part you played, and what you want to do next belong in the same view. This might involve acknowledging a mistake, choosing a different direction, or accepting that you have changed. Alongside concern about how others will judge you, ask which facts already support a decision.

Reversed, the card may describe knowing a reply is needed but delaying through endless preparation. It can also suggest turning reflection into relentless self-blame, leaving no room to act again. Distinguish “I still need information” from “I have enough information, but fear taking responsibility for the consequences”. The first calls for further checking; the second for smaller steps you can take responsibility for.

## In everyday situations

**Career.** After a period in a role, you become increasingly certain that you do not want to keep doing the same duties. Write down the relevant experiences, acceptable conditions and possible next steps, then decide whether to discuss changes or explore another direction.

**Repairing a relationship.** You realise that an earlier response hurt a friend. Renewal can begin by acknowledging the specific behaviour and hearing how it affected them. Saying “I understand now” does not entitle you to immediate forgiveness.

**A review.** A project ends, and everyone wants to move on quickly. Describe recurring mistakes and agree who will take responsibility in future. That gives reflection a new outcome, rather than making one person the target of every accusation.

## Try it for yourself

Write a five-sentence reply to your future self: what happened, what you acknowledge, what you will stop excusing, what you can repair, and when you will take the first step. Keep each sentence about actions, rather than labels for your character.

## Common misreadings

Judgement does not pronounce you guilty, or guarantee the return of an old relationship or a particular person. Rising again can help us think about renewal, but reconciliation in real life still requires both people’s willingness.

## Read these cards together

- Justice: Compare weighing responsibility against facts with Judgement’s emphasis on review, response and renewal.
- Death: Compare the ending of a stage with the answer you give to a new life after it.
- The World: Notice how a definite response can lead towards completing a stage.

## Sources and further reading

- A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Part II, XX: [English text](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar20.htm)
- The same book, Part III, Section 3, entry 20: [original upright and reversed meanings](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)
- Pamela Colman Smith, RWS card: [Commons image and version history](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_20_Judgement.jpg)

The English transcription is dated 1911; the image page identifies the card as Pam-A, 1910. The visual description follows the downloaded Commons JPG. The modern quick takes and exercises are DestinyPixel's original interpretations. Sources checked: 2026-10-07.

sourceRecord.title: 审判 听清该回应的事
sourceRecord.hook: 号角响起，所有人都抬起头；这次，问题是你准备怎样回应。

quickTake.upright: 有些事不能再含糊，该回头看清，再作决定了
quickTake.reversed: 迟迟不肯回应，或反复责怪自己，卡在决定之前

sections.title: 谁在发声，谁在回答
paragraphs: 上方的天使从云中显现，红色双翼向两边展开，吹响一支向下的金色号角。号角上垂着白底红十字的旗帜。下方的灰白色人物从打开的长方形棺中站起，仰头伸手，动作共同指向天空。
前景左边是成人，右边是另一位成人，中间较小的人物背对观者；更远处还有一组同样伸展双臂的人。水面与起伏山脉把场景拉得很深。因此，这不是某个人单独站在台前挨训的构图。号角发出的召唤，与众人向上回应的身体，构成一场集体的转变。[查看审判牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_20_Judgement.jpg)。

sections.title: 名字来自审判，Waite 关注转变
paragraphs: Waite 在第二部沿用末日审判与复活的宗教意象，但特别强调人物共同呈现惊奇、敬拜与欣喜。他进一步把它解释为回应更高召唤而完成的转变，并认为召唤也从内在被听见、被回应。这是他的神秘主义诠释，不能直接当成读者收到超自然命令。[Waite 的审判篇](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar20.htm)。
第三部占辞列有位置变化、更新、结果；逆位中既有软弱，也有深思、决定等词，并非单一的惩罚。[Waite 的占辞](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)。

sections.title: 回顾，是为了作出新的回答
paragraphs: 本站把正位读成一个需要正式回应的节点。过去发生了什么、你承担了什么、接下来想怎样做，需要放到一起看。它可能涉及承认错误、重新选择方向，或接受自己已经变了。与其只问别人会如何评价你，不如问现在有哪些事实已经足够支持决定。
逆位可以是明知需要答复，却用继续准备拖延；也可能是把检讨变成无休止的自责，始终不肯给自己一次重新行动的机会。分清“还有资料缺失”与“资料已经够了，我只是害怕承担后果”。前者继续核实，后者需要把大决定拆成能负责的小步。

situations.title: 职业
situations.text: 做完一段工作后，越来越清楚自己不愿继续同样的职责。把具体经历、能接受的条件和下一步选择写下来，再决定要谈调整还是寻找其他方向。

situations.title: 修复关系
situations.text: 你意识到之前的回应伤了朋友。审判式的更新可以从承认具体行为、听对方的感受开始；一句“我已经想通了”并不能要求对方立刻原谅。

situations.title: 复盘
situations.text: 项目结束，大家只想赶快翻篇。把可重复的失误讲清、明确以后由谁负责，才让回顾产生新的结果，而不是寻找一个人承担所有指责。

sourceRecord.practice: 给未来的自己写一段五句话的回信：发生了什么、我承认什么、我不再替什么找借口、我能修正什么、何时迈第一步。每句尽量落到行为，避免给自己贴人格标签。
sourceRecord.commonMisread: 审判不是“你有罪”的宣告，也不保证旧情复燃或某人回来。牌里的重新站起可以帮助理解更新，但现实中的和解仍需双方愿意参与。

relatedCards.reason: 比较依据事实衡量责任，与审判更突出的回顾、回应和更新。
比较一个阶段的结束，与结束之后对新生活作出回答。
观察正式回应怎样接向一个阶段的完成。
